evals.name: slice-review-report
evals.expected_output: Starts with a one-line Review result (Changes requested). Blocking: business rejection thrown instead of returned as ValidationResult/validator (500 not validation error); event carries the event-source id; built-in exception type. Also raw Guid/string rather than concepts/EventSourceId; == null; missing XML docs. Each blocking item names a consequence and gives a fix; states what was not reviewed.
assertions: Opens with a single-line review result of the form Approved, Approved with comments, or Changes requested, and picks Changes requested.
Flags the throw from Handle as blocking because it becomes an HTTP 500 instead of a validation error, and recommends a validator or ValidationResult.
Flags the event carrying the event-source id (BoatId) and the use of a built-in exception type.
Flags raw Guid and string instead of concept types, with identity derived from EventSourceId<T> rather than ConceptAs<Guid>.
Names the consequence for blocking findings and says what was not reviewed.

evals.name: red-build-and-severity
evals.prompt: A teammate asks you to review a change but `dotnet build` fails with two analyzer errors and one spec is red. They want a full style report anyway, and they mark every finding as blocking so nothing is prioritized. How should the review proceed and how should findings be classified? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Run the gates first; a gate failure is the finding and the review stops since there is nothing to review under a red build. Do not restate compiler/analyzer output as review findings. Separate blocking from suggestions with consequences; if everything blocks nothing is prioritized.
assertions: Says gates (build, specifications, lint) are run first and a gate failure is reported as the finding with the review stopping.
Says a review should not restate what the compiler or analyzer already reports.
Says blocking issues must be separated from suggestions, and that treating everything as blocking prioritizes nothing.
Says a blocking finding names a consequence rather than just citing a rule.

evals.name: singleton-scoped-dependency
evals.prompt: In review: `[Singleton] public class BoatCatalog(IEventStore eventStore, IMongoCollection<Boat> boats)`; the event store call is used in a handler. Also an untouched line elsewhere in the same file still uses `== null`. What do you report and how severe is each? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: A [Singleton] must not take a scoped dependency such as the event store or a MongoDB collection/database/client; make the type transient or scoped (IServiceScopeFactory only for a service the host resolves once). A pre-existing violation in a line the change did not touch is a note, never a blocker.
assertions: Flags the singleton taking the event store and a MongoDB collection as a blocking finding.
Recommends making the type transient or scoped instead.
Says a pre-existing violation on a line the change did not touch is a note, not a blocker.

evals.name: spec-coverage-review
evals.prompt: The change adds a command with one validation rule, one business-rule rejection and a unique constraint. The specs: a happy-path spec, a validation spec asserting only the error message text 'Name is required', a spec for a property getter, and a Thread.Sleep(500) before an assertion. Review the specification coverage. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Validation failure spec must assert both ShouldNotBeSuccessful() and ShouldHaveValidationErrors(); message strings are not asserted by default; missing spec for business-rule rejection; missing EventScenario spec asserting the constraint name; trivial getter spec should not exist; no sleeping.
assertions: Says the validation failure specification must assert both ShouldNotBeSuccessful() and ShouldHaveValidationErrors().
Says presentation message strings are not asserted by default.
Flags the missing business-rule rejection specification and the missing EventScenario constraint specification asserting the constraint name.
Flags the trivial property getter specification and the sleep in a specification.

evals.name: routing-and-convention-vs-contract
evals.prompt: While reviewing, a teammate says 'the framework requires every slice to be in its own folder and requires a single file per slice' and asks you to also include a full security audit and a deep replay-performance analysis in the same report. How do you handle it? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Slice folder shape and single-file default are house conventions, not framework contracts; Handle() on the record and [Path] are contracts. Don't call a convention a framework requirement. A focused security audit goes to cratis-security-review; scalability analysis to cratis-performance-review; do not restate specialist performance findings; only flag visible performance items in passing.
assertions: Says the slice folder shape and single-file default are house conventions, not framework contracts.
Names Handle() on the record or the [Path] attribute as framework contracts.
Routes a focused security audit to the security review skill and a scalability analysis to the performance review skill.
Says the report states what was not reviewed.

evals.name: follow-up-round-is-delta
evals.prompt: You reviewed a change earlier at commit a1b2c3d and reported one blocker: RegisterBoat.Handle threw an exception for a missing name. The author pushed commit e4f5a6b that moves the check into a CommandValidator and touches nothing else. Give the follow-up review report in your reply (do not write files).
evals.expected_output: A follow-up round that reviews only the delta since a1b2c3d, says whether the earlier blocker is resolved, does not re-review untouched files, and states what was not re-examined.
assertions: Scopes the review to the changes since the previously reviewed commit rather than the whole change.
States whether the earlier blocker is resolved, citing the validator change.
Does not raise new findings about files the author did not touch.
Says what was not re-examined in this round.
